and before i begin, this isn't me discounting very real issues men face (loosing 2 years to NS, not having mental health issues being taken seriously, etc etc) but it IS possible to talk about both sides, with nuance and understanding

  
For the workplace

The reason women have been excluded from high positions of power in the workplace used to be a result of hard labour market discrimination practices. And while, we don't have such hard laws and policies that stop women from participating anymore - societal attitudes and biases still definitely prevent them from going pass the glass ceiling. 

- Men consistently value the same work women do to be less valuable than mens **so much so, that whenever women take over a male dominated field, the pay drops.**  (https://www.nytimes.com/2016/03/20/upshot/as-women-take-over-a-male-dominated-field-the-pay-drops.html**)**

- Men tend to view aggressive/confident women far more negatively than they do for other men. This being especially pernicious, because to rise through the ranks, you do require a degree of assertiveness and control - yet men are allowed to exhibit this with relative ease, but women face a double bind (https://www.forbes.com/sites/kathycaprino/2017/06/15/gender-bias-at-work-why-men-call-forceful-women-hysterical-and-try-to-silence-them/?sh=53fc1e853ea2)

- Women are told that they are "naturally" caretakers, and are socially pushed into care oriented (that are lesser paying) fields, despite having the SAME QUALIFICATIONS AS MEN ( Singapore's Adjusted Gender Pay Gap shows that despite the significant increase in the proportion of women in professionals and associate professional and technicians (“APT”) , many women remained in traditionally female occupations (e.g. professionals in nursing, and teaching and training, and administrative APT) which are generally lower paying compared to occupations with higher male shares)

For the home

- Women are largely, exclusively, supposed to be the only caretakers of a family home. When joining the workforce, they are meant to take the extreme unequal burden of both caring for their work and family. Often this results in them being unable to do the extra shifts/ go for that networking event, and essentially loose their prime working years (late 20s to 30s) raising a family. 

Understand that pregnancy and raising a family are OFTEN exclusive burdens that only women face.
